# Plan: SPE round r01, triage agent

Your prompt is the spec. This plan is the r01 prediction. After you approve it, I save the plan and the prediction and commit them locally. Then I build the agent and the harness, pass the gates, and launch one Workflow run as the eval. I never push or tag on a remote. Commits are local and carry no Claude attribution.

The spec leaves the ticket data, the categories, and the meaning of "cheaply" open. I picked a default for each, listed under 1.2, and each one goes into `spe/spec/disagreements.md` with you as owner.

## 1. Specify

### 1.1 Requirement table (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent reads one ticket (subject and body) and returns JSON with `category`, `priority`, `needs_human`, and `reason`. | Decision D1 | `check_schema` validates every output against `triage/schema.json` |
| R2 | The agent picks the right category. | User: "triage tickets correctly" | `check_category`: exact match with the answer key, accuracy at least 0.85 on the test split |
| R3 | The agent picks the right priority. | User: "correctly" | `check_priority`: exact match, accuracy at least 0.70 |
| R4 | The agent does not miss urgent tickets. | User: "correctly", plus decision D3 | `check_p1_recall`: P1 recall at least 0.90 |
| R5 | Triage is cheap. | User: "cheaply", plus decision D4 | `check_cost`: mean cost per ticket at most $0.005, computed from API token usage and the pinned prices |
| R6 | Output is always usable. | Decision D1 | `check_schema`: valid rate at least 0.98. An invalid output counts as wrong on R2 to R4. |
| R7 | The agent never sees test answers. | Way rule | `check_no_leak`: no overlap between few-shot examples and the test split by ticket ID or text hash, and a scan of every prompt sent for answer-key strings |

A configuration passes the spec when it meets R2 through R6.

### 1.2 Defaults (logged in `disagreements.md`, owner: you)

| ID | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | The agent is a Python 3.12 module at `triage/agent.py`. It calls the Anthropic Messages API with no tools and reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment. I never print the key. | There is no existing code, and the API returns token usage, which R5 needs. |
| D2 | There are 6 categories: `billing`, `bug`, `outage`, `account_access`, `feature_request`, `how_to`. There are 4 priorities, P1 to P4. | This is a common support-desk taxonomy. |
| D3 | Data is 160 synthetic tickets: a 120-ticket test split (20 per category, 18 at P1) and a 40-ticket dev split. A separate Opus subagent writes them from a generator brief. That subagent never sees the agent prompts. | No real tickets exist in the repo. |
| D4 | "Cheaply" means a mean cost of at most $0.005 per ticket. I take prices from the Anthropic pricing docs on run day and save them in `spe/evals/harness/prices.json`. | This is a placeholder number. You may want a different one. |
| D5 | Each test ticket runs 2 times per configuration. | Two repeats show unstable answers at low cost. |

### 1.3 Open decisions (owner: you, r01 proceeds on the default)

- O1: Should real tickets replace the synthetic set? With synthetic labels, accuracy only measures agreement with another model's labels.
- O2: Does the D2 taxonomy match your queue?
- O3: Is $0.005 per ticket the right cost target?
- O4: Configuration C tests a Haiku-tier model as the system under test. The house rule against picking Haiku covers subagents that do work, not models under test. Reject C at approval if you do not want it.

## 2. Predict

### 2.1 Configurations (one change each from A)

| Config | Model | Prompt | Change from A |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Sonnet-tier, model ID pinned from current docs at build time | System prompt with category and priority definitions, zero-shot | None (baseline) |
| B | Same as A | A plus 12 few-shot examples from the dev split, 2 per category | Adds few-shot examples |
| C | Haiku-tier, model ID pinned from current docs | Same as A | Cheaper model |

### 2.2 Numeric prediction

A hit is a measured value inside the band. This is round 1, so there is no "same as last round" column. The naive guess for close-out is "B and C score the same as A".

| Metric | A | B | C | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | 0.85 ± 0.05 | 0.89 ± 0.04 | 0.78 ± 0.06 | `check_category` | The synthetic tickets are clean. Bug and outage will blur, and so will how_to and account_access. Examples sharpen those edges. A smaller model blurs them more. |
| Priority exact match | 0.70 ± 0.08 | 0.75 ± 0.07 | 0.62 ± 0.08 | `check_priority` | P2 and P3 are a judgment call, so priority runs about 15 points below category. |
| P1 recall | 0.90 ± 0.06 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.82 ± 0.08 | `check_p1_recall` | Outage wording is loud and easy to catch. With 18 P1 tickets, one miss moves recall by 0.056. |
| Schema valid rate | 0.99 ± 0.01 | 0.99 ± 0.01 | 0.97 ± 0.03 | `check_schema` | The schema is enforced in the request. A smaller model drifts slightly more often. |
| Mean cost per ticket (USD) | 0.004 ± 0.0015 | 0.009 ± 0.003 | 0.0013 ± 0.0005 | `check_cost` | I assume about 900 input tokens and 80 output tokens per call at about $3 and $15 per million tokens for Sonnet and $1 and $5 for Haiku. The examples add about 1,800 input tokens. These prices are estimates until the docs check. |

Derived prediction: A barely passes the spec. B fails R5 on cost. C fails R2 and R3.

## 3. Evaluate

### 3.1 After approval, before anything else

1. Save your prompt and planning answers verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`. Write `spe/spec/spec.md` with the table in 1.1, `spe/spec/disagreements.md` with 1.2 and 1.3, and a skeleton `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 specify: triage spec from plan-mode prompt`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds `round: 1`, `date: 2026-10-21`, `author: "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode"`, the three configs, every number from 2.2 with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round: null`. Commit `SPE r01 predict: 3 configs, category accuracy 0.78 to 0.89`.

### 3.2 Build and harness steps

| Step | Work | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Build `triage/agent.py`, `triage/schema.json`, and `triage/configs/{A,B,C}.yaml`. Commit `triage: agent with configs A, B, C`. | One live call per config returns valid JSON. |
| 4 | A separate Opus subagent writes `spe/evals/data/tickets_test.jsonl`, `tickets_dev.jsonl`, and `answers.jsonl` from `spe/evals/data/generator-brief.md`. | Counts match D3. `check_no_leak` finds no dev and test overlap. |
| 5 | Write `spe/evals/harness/grade.py` with the five checks and `check_no_leak`. Write `spe/evals/harness/run_trials.py`. Save `prices.json` from the docs. | None yet. |
| 6 | Grader selftest. | The oracle (answers as outputs) scores 1.0 on R2 to R4. Empty outputs fail every check. Shifted wrong labels score below 0.20. |
| 7 | Control. No earlier round exists, so the control is a regrade of `spe/evals/harness/fixtures/control.jsonl`. That file has 10 hand-labeled outputs with known scores. | The regrade reproduces the known scores exactly. |
| 8 | Write `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` with `const ROUND = 1`. All prompt text reads the round from it. | A dry run on cells A×outage, B×bug, and C×how_to completes and grades. |
| 9 | Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness): dataset, grader, workflow`. Launch the Workflow. | Every gate above passed. |

### 3.3 Workflow design and arguments

- Arguments: `configs: ["A","B","C"]`, `split: "test"`, `repeats: 2`, `extra_repeats_per_ticket: 2`, `extra_calls_cap: 120`, `api_spend_cap_usd: 10`, `results_dir: "spe/evals/results/r01/"`.
- Phase 1 runs trials per config. Each trial is one API call with the ticket text only. Every output follows the schema.
- Phase 2 grades with code only. No judge is needed this round, because every requirement has a code check.
- Phase 3 runs `check_no_leak` over every prompt sent and voids any trial that contains answer-key text. Trials have no tools, so they cannot read files.
- Phase 4 is split cells. When a ticket's 2 repeats disagree, it gets up to 2 more repeats within `extra_calls_cap`.
- The harness checks the spend running total before each call. It skips any call that would cross `api_spend_cap_usd` and logs the skip.
- Phase 5 is failure analysis. An Opus agent groups wrong answers into F-numbered failure types with examples.
- Phase 6 is a completeness critic. An Opus agent confirms that every predicted cell has a measured number and that voids and skips are logged.

### 3.4 Cost estimate (unmeasured)

- Triage API calls: about 240 calls per config, plus up to 120 extra calls. That is about $1.00 for A, $2.20 for B, $0.30 for C, and up to $0.60 for extras, for a total near $4. The hard cap is $10.
- Session tokens: the dataset author, failure analysis, and critic agents run on Opus. I estimate 300k to 600k tokens billed to the session. This is a guess.

### 3.5 Halt and report

I stop and report to you if the spend cap is hit, if an answer key leaks into a prompt, if a grader gate fails, or if a decision only you can make comes up.

## 4. Learn (when the Workflow completion notice arrives)

1. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>` with `spe/evals/results/r01/`.
2. Write `spe/prediction-log.md` with the columns Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under the table, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. I say plainly if the naive guess beat my predictions.
3. Write `spe/failures.md`. Each new type gets a name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure, and its original and regraded numbers sit side by side.
4. Add a "Proposed for round 2" table to `spe/spec/spec.md`. A likely row is "B with prompt caching", to test whether examples can pass R5. Write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
5. Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 learn: <summary>` and tag `spe-r01` locally.

The loop stops after 3 rounds in a row where predictions match results. If every config passes everything, round 2 needs harder tickets or stricter graders.
